finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.ts::webhook accepts an epoch-zero / go zero-time `issuedat` and turns it into a permanent no-op instead of falling back to now()
evidence: Verified at yorkie-event.controller.ts:55-58: only `Number.isNaN(issuedMs)` falls back to `now()`, so a parseable epoch-zero (`1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` → 0) or Go zero-time (`0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` → negative) passes through `Math.min` intact. `DocumentService.touchUpdatedAt` then filters `where: { updatedAt: { lt: at } }`, which can never match because the column defaults to `now()` / is backfilled to `createdAt`, so the event is silently dropped and 200-swallowed. The claimed sibling guard is real too: `yorkie-admin.service.ts` `parseTimestamp` rejects `ms <= 0` as Yorkie's "unset", and `yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts` has no zero-timestamp case. I could not confirm from this tree whether Yorkie 0.7.12 actually emits a zero `issuedAt`, so the trigger likelihood (and hence blast radius) is unverified, but the missing guard and its consequence are exactly as described.
